A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same dynamic weight-grafting study, with matchable experiments, equations, figures and appendices. V2 contains several truncated result paragraphs, but the corresponding plots remain available and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original finetuning and weight-grafting experiments on four language models, including position-level and component-level results in Figures 2–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experimental results and reports additional top-k sensitivity, movie-title grafting and unembedding comparisons in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The token-wise, component-wise weight-swapping method, grafting mask and KV-cache procedure remain the same. V2's pseudocode documents the existing procedure; the additional grafting configurations and unembedding comparisons are experimental analyses.

E1.justification: The three synthetic datasets and relation-completion task are retained. V2 explicitly evaluates movie-title-containing prompts in C.5, but v1 Figure 13c already reports an undefined 'Test Sentence 3'. The PDFs do not establish whether this represents new input-scenario coverage or expanded analysis of an existing scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the pretrained and supervised-finetuned reference models and existing grafting comparisons. Newly cited interpretability and editing methods are not evaluated as additional baselines; movie-title and unembedding variants are internal ablations.

E3.justification: V2 adds scoring at k=1, 10 and 100, movie-title-specific grafting configurations, and a finetuned-versus-pretrained unembedding comparison. The stated model sizes, 80/20 train/validation split and two finetuning regimes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses in C.2, C.5 and C.6 test whether pathway findings depend on the accuracy threshold, whether movie-title tokens support retrieval alone or jointly with entity/final-token grafts, and whether output unembeddings affect localization. These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence. Earlier less-aggressive-finetuning, component-grafting and token-probability analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both retain the same '3 training runs' wording in the compute estimate. Removing v1's checklist declaration about absent error bars does not change the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Shared main-result plots retain their values, while v2 adds substantial results for the new analyses. For example, Figure 16 reports Gemma accuracy of 0.94 for movie-title-plus-last-token grafting versus 0.72 for last-token grafting on the movie-title prompt. Figure 17 reports first-entity accuracy of 0.23 with finetuned unembeddings versus 0.13 with pretrained unembeddings. These supplement the retained results under additional configurations.

T1.justification: V2 removes v1's directional-patching projection equation and its explicit connection to dynamic grafting. The displayed Transformer-block equation also removes the outer LayerNorm and accommodates LayerNorm or RMSNorm. These are limited changes to mathematical exposition; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central enrichment/recall pathways and component-localization claims remain. V2 additionally states applicability to pretrained/finetuned model pairs across most post-training procedures and asserts more categorically that activation patching combined with ablations cannot establish the required necessity and sufficiency; v1 described localization as difficult.

C2.justification: V2 characterizes measured retrieval accuracy as a lower bound, interprets the added sensitivity analyses, and adds qualifications about generalization across contexts and potentially different mechanisms in larger models. V1's discussion of FFN up/down projections as read/write operations is omitted, although the corresponding results remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds dynamic-grafting pseudocode in A.1, explicit unidirectional training examples in A.2.4, the movie-title evaluation template, and a reproducibility/LLM-usage statement. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, timing estimates and the code URL remain; the PDFs do not establish a new resource release.

R1.justification: V2 expands citations concerning knowledge editing, component localization and weight-space knowledge regions, including De Cao et al., Meng et al. 2022b, Kramar et al. and Gueta et al. Dedicated directional-patching and causal-mediation references are removed. The overall positioning around mechanistic localization of finetuned knowledge remains.

P1.justification: The title and terminology shift from relation extraction to knowledge retrieval/relation completion. The abstract, introduction and methodology are extensively rewritten; background and method sections are consolidated, discussion is reorganized, a reproducibility section is added, and the checklist is removed. V2 also introduces three visibly truncated result paragraphs.

P2.justification: V2 adds an activation-patching comparison schematic, revises and relocates existing diagrams, reduces main Figure 2 to two model panels while retaining other results in the appendix, and adds examples to Table 1. Five appendix figures present additional analyses. Figure 12's caption incorrectly says top-10 despite its top-100 heading and axes.

improvement.justification: The added top-k and unembedding controls strengthen confidence that the pathway findings are not confined to the original evaluation choices. Pseudocode and explicit training examples also improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh localized presentation losses because the original plots remain available, but truncated result paragraphs in Sections 3.1 and 3.3 and the mislabeled Figure 12 limit the overall improvement.
